detectors.rationale: Assigning attacker-influenceable data (an API-sourced comment body) to .innerHTML parses it as markup and executes any embedded script/event-handler, a classic DOM XSS sink; the safe idiom assigns to .textContent, which the browser always treats as literal text and never parses as markup.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React's auto-escaping and injects the given __html string as raw markup, so an attacker-controlled profile bio can carry a script/onerror payload; the safe idiom uses ordinary JSX interpolation ({userBio}), which React always renders as an escaped text node.

Passing a user-typed search-box expression to eval() grants it full script execution in the page's origin; the safe idiom replaces eval with a grammar-limited parser function that only recognizes a fixed set of comparison operators and never reaches the JS engine's code evaluator.

document.write() concatenated with a query-string-derived campaign name streams attacker-controlled markup directly into the document parser, enabling script injection; the safe idiom builds a DOM element and assigns the untrusted value via .textContent, which is never parsed as HTML.

Interpolating a user-saved template string into new Function(...) compiles attacker-controlled text into an executable function body, equivalent to eval; the safe idiom looks up a fixed key in a statically defined map of precompiled formatter functions, so no user-supplied text is ever compiled.
